Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials

During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items

Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent Calendar,
individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion of these

removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members of the
public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three (3)
minutes in total.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

  6
 Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

 PUBLIC  NOTIFICATION
Advertising  and notification  of the public  hearing  for this item was conducted  in compliance  with
Sections  11.50.020  and 11.50.030  of the South  Gate Municipal  Code ("SGMC").  Notices  of the
hearing  were posted  and published  in the "South  Gate Press"  on April  10, 2025.

ENVIRONMENT  AL  EV ALUATION
In accordance  with  the California  Environmental  Quality  Act  ("CEQA"),  the City  Council's
deten'nination  qualifies  for a categorical  exemption  under CEQA  Guidelines  Section  15321,  (Class
21) "Enforcement  Actions  by Regulatory  Agencies,"  in that the City  of South  Gate ("City")  is
enforcing  the South Gate Municipal  Code.

The City  Council's  determination  on the extension  of TUP  No. 2020-01  is not subject  to CEQA
review  because  it is not an "approval"  as defined  in California  Code  of Regulations,  Title  14,
Section  15352,  but rather  a determination  of whether  a use must terminate  at a site, and therefore
does not coinrnit  the City  to any definite  course  of action  regarding  new uses or changes  to the
approved  use of the subject  property.  Furthermore,  CEQA  does not apply  to projects  which  a
public  agency  rejects  or disapproves  pursuant  to Section  15270(a).

BACKGROUND
This is an appeal  filed  by legal counsel,  Somos  Law  Group  ("Somos"),  on behalf  of the property
owner  and applicant,  Alameda  Engle  Properties,  LLC  ("AEP"  represented  by Jason Engle),  for a
6.78-acre  property  located  at  8530  Alameda  Street.  Somos  is  appealing  the  Planning
Commission's  decision  on the Director  of Community  Development's  determination.

It should  be noted that AEP  also owns  the abutting  2.9-acre  site to the north  at 8440 S. Alameda
Street,  which  is located  outside  of the City  and in the County  of Los Angeles.  Access  to both
properties  is via a driveway  from  Alameda  Street to the property  at 8440 S. Alameda  Street. This
property  is also being  used for truck  trailer  storage  and according  to County  staff,  a conditional
use permit  ("CUP")  is cunently  being  processed.

History  of Zoning and Land Use of Subiect Property
As early  as 1961,  the Subject  Property  was designated  as being  within  a Heavy  Manufacturing
("M-3")  Zone.

Based  upon  a review  of public  records  and documents  submitted  by AEP,  the Site was used by
JackEngel  & Company(hereinafter,  "JECO")  and/orAEP  forametalprocessingrecyclingfacility
from  as early  as 1973 until  approximately  March  2020.  During  that time,  the site was developed
with a single-story  industrial  structure  used for the recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO and/or
AEP.

The metal  recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO  and/or  AEP  included,  but was not limited  to,
the delivery  of scrap metal product  to the Site inside  of truck  trailers  - which  would  remain  on site
for up to several  months  while  the scrap metal  was sorted and processed  on-site,  and prepared  for
shipment  to a final  off-site  destination.

AS13772.0860893  4909-8288-0805vl

  9
 In 1988,  the  City  amended  its  Zoning  Code,  in part,  to require  a Conditional  Use  Permit  for
recycling  facilities.  Thereafter,  on or about  April  28, 2015,  the City  Council  adopted  Ordinance
2323,  which  further  amended  the Zoning  Code  and changed  the zoning  classification  of the Subject
Property  to Industrial  Flex  ("IF")  Zone.

Pursuant  to the  Section  11.21.030  and Table  11.21-3  of the  amended  Zoning  Code,  recycling
facilities  require  a Conditional  Use  Permit  -  however,  the recycling  operations  at the  Subject
Property  were  deemed  to be a legal,  nonconforming  land  use that  was  allowed  to continue  in
accordance  with  SGMC  Chapter  11.55  ("Nonconforming  Uses and Buildings").

According  to public  records  and information  submitted  by AEP  and/or  its representatives,  all metal
recycling  operations  ceased  in or around  March  2020  and are no longer  being  conducted  at the
Site.

AEP  has confirmed  that around  March  2020,  Fleet  Yards,  Inc. commenced  utilizing  the Site solely
for the storage  of truck  trailers  and/or  containers  as a principal  use.  Moreover,  the stmcture  that
was previously  utilized  to conduct  the metal  recycling  at the Site was demolished.

On July  16, 2020,  the City  approved  Fleet  Yards,  Inc.'s  application  for  a Temporary  Use Permit
and issued  TUP2020-01,  authorizing  the use of the Subject  Property  for "truck  trailer  storage  for
a one-year  period  with  possible  one-year  extensions  up to a maximum  period  of five  years  from
the  date  of  approval".  The  Community  Development  Director  explicitly  imposed  various
conditions  upon  the approval  of TUP2020-01,  including,  but not limited  to:

  1.  The  approved  temporary  use for the Site is restricted  to truck  trailer  storage  only  - and
  no other  use is permitted  without  the written  authorization  from  the City.

  2.  The  approval  of the temporary  use was  set to expire  on July  16,  2021  - and  a new
  application  was to be submitted  at least  thirty  (30)  days  prior  to the expiration  date if
  an extension  was  desired.  Additional  one-year  extensions  would  be considered  for
  approval  for up to a maximum  period  of 5 years  from  the original  approval  date of July
  16,  2020  -  and would  be determined  based  upon  compliance  with  the  conditions  of
  approval  and written  verification  from  the property  owner  that the owner  is in process
  of developing  the land,  selling  the land,  and/or  working  with  Los Angeles  Community
  College  or a developer  on a housing  development  project.

TUP2020-01  expired  on July 16, 2021,  without  a timely  request  for renewal  from  Fleet  Yards,  Inc.

On or about  July  11, 2022,  an e-mail  was  submitted  to the Planning  Division  requesting  a new
Temporary  Use Permit  (or the renewal  of TUP2020-01).  In December  2022,  the Director  advised
Fleet  Yards,  Inc.  that  several  conditions  of approval  of the TUP  had  not  been  adhered  to, and,
moreover,  that the TUP  was ineligible  for renewal  as SGMC  § 11.51.070(B)(4)  sets the maximum
duration  of Temporary  Use Permits  to no more  than three  days in a row  or ten working  days in any
calendar  year.

AS13772.0860893  4909-8288-0805vl

  10
 Planning  Commission  Hearing
On May  2, 2023,  the Planning  Coinrnission  conducted  a public  hearing  on the appeal  of the
Director  of Community  Development's  determination  to deny an extension  of TUP No. 2020-01
for a truck  trailer  storage  at 8530 Alameda  Street.

The appellant's  attorney,  Alfred  Fraijo  Jr., gave a presentation  on the basis of the appeal.  Public
comment  was received  from  the following  individuals:

  *  Alan  Engle  (property  owner,  Alameda  Engle  & Company)
  *  Daniel  Otting  (Fleet Yard  Inc., 8440 S. Alameda  st., Los Angeles)
  *  Jennifer  Ganata  (6325  Pacific  Boulevard,  Ste. 300, Huntington  Park)

The Planning  Commission  also received  a presentation  by City  staff and outside  legal counsel
James Eckart  providing  a response  to the appellant's  presentation.

At the conclusion  of the hearing,  the Planning  Commission  voted  3-2 to adopt Resolution  No.
2023-05  denying  the appeal  and upholding  the Director's  Determination.  In reaching  its decision,
the Planning  Commission  specifically  determined  that:

  1.  The land use of storage  of truck  trailers  and containers  is not authorized  or allowed  by the
  South Gate Municipal  Code on any land within  the Industrial  Flex  (IF) zone, of which  the
  subject  property  is a part.

  2.  Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01  was originally  issued  in error  and in violation  of City
  ordinances.  Temporary  use permits  are to be used for "short-term  activities"  which  are of
  a "short-term  nature."  In  addition,  the  South  Gate  Municipal  Code  specifies  that  the
  maximum  duration  of a temporary  use permit  shall not exceed  three days in a row,  or ten
  working  days in any calendar  year. Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01  was issued in error as
  the approval  was granted  for a longer  period  of time than the South  Gate Municipal  Code
  allows  for.

Following  the Planning  Coinmission's  meeting,  the applicant  met with  staff to discuss  options  in
dealing  with  the situation  which  ultimately  led to a second  determination  by the Community
Development  Director  on the legal  nonconforming  status  and a request  for a zone change  and
General  Plan Amendment,  which  are being  processed  separately  from  this request.

ANALYSIS:

The renewal  application  was denied  because  under  the SGMC:  (1) the use which  is the subject  of
the Temporary  Use Permit  is prohibited  at 8530 Alameda;  and (2) Temporary  Use Permits  can
only allow  otherwise  unauthorized  uses to be conducted  for a few days, not for multi-year  periods.

Past/Proposed  Use of Property  is as a "Truck  Storage/Terminal":  Applicant  and its tenant  have
been using  the subject  property  to store trucks,  truck-trailers,  and storage  containers.  Under  the
SGMC,  this use is defined  as "truck  storage/terminal"  use which,  pursuant  to the SGMC  Section
11.60.230  "T"  definitions,  "means  indoor  or outdoor  site for freight,  truck  terminals,  truck  storage
yards,  or similar  commercial  facilities."

AS13772.0860893  4909-8288-0805vl

  11
   SGMC  Prohibits  that Use at 8530 Alameda  Street:  The subject  property  is zoned  Industrial  Flex
  (IF). Table 11.21-3,  under  SGMC  Section  11.21.030  "Land  use permissions  tables",  lists allowed
  land uses within  the IF zone. Truck  storage/terminal  use is not listed  on that Table  as an allowed
  use within  the IF zone.  SGMC  Section  11.21.020  notes that "Any  land use that is not specifically
  listed  in the land use tables  for the applicable  zone shall not be allowed  or permitted  within  the
  zone."  Therefore,  the storage  of trucks,  truck-trailers  and containers  is a prohibited  use in the IF
  zone.

  Temporary  Use Permits  Cannot  Authorize  Prohibited  Uses for Extended  Durations.  Pursuant  to
  SGMC  Section  11.51.070  "Temporary  Use  Permit,"  temporary  use  permits  are processed
  administratively  to "allow  for short-term  activities  that warrant  individual  consideration  and are
  acceptable  because  of  their  temporary,  short-term  nature."  SGMC  Section  11.51.070  (A)
  "Temporary  Uses,"  also notes that the "provisions  of this section  shall regulate  all special  events
  and temporary  land uses as permitted  by Table  11.21-3,  11.21-4,  or 11.21-5,  as applicable  to the
  zone, or as deternnined  by the director."  SGMC  Section  11.51.010  (B) lists "Mandatory  Approval
  Conditions"  for temporary  use permits,  wherein  there are "limits  on the maximum  duration  will
  be specified  in the permit,  and shall  not exceed  three days in a row,  or ten working  days in any
  calendar  year."

  Original  Issuance  of the TUP was Done in Error,  and Renewal  of the TUP is not authorized  by the
  SGMC.  Based  on limitations  imposed  by the South  Gate Municipal  Code upon  the issuance  of
  Temporary  Use Permits  as set forth  hereinabove,  and notwithstanding  the language  contained
  within  TUP2020-01,  the Director  of Community  Development  was prohibited  from  granting  an
  extension  of TUP2020-01.  The Plaru'iing  Commission  was similarly  prohibited  from  granting  an
  extension  of TUP2020-01  for similar  reasons  and upheld  the Director's  Determination.

  Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01  should  never have been issued in the first place for the purported
  use (which  is prohibited  within  the IF Zone)  nor forthe  duration  set forth therein,  since itpurported
  to authorize  the subject  use for one year (with  possible  extensions  for a total  of 5 years from  the
  original  date  of  issuance),  which  is  far  longer  than  the  three-consecutive-day  and  ten-
  nonconsecutive-day  maximum  periods  autliorized  by the SGMC.

  Notwithstanding  the pending  appeal,  there  is no authority  in the South  Gate Municipal  Code to
  authorize  an extension  of  TUP2020-01  for  the  use  or time  period  that  was  originally  and
  erroneously  approved.  As such, the appeal must be denied.

  CONCLUSION
  Staff  recommends  the City  Council  uphold  the Planning  Commission's  decision  to uphold  the
  Director's  Determination  to deny an extension  of TUP No. 2020-01  for truck-trailer  storage  at the
  subject  property.

In  accordance  with  the  California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA),  the  City  Council's

The  City  Council's  determination  on the termination  of the legal,  non-conforming  use of the

City  to any definite  course  of action  regarding  new uses or changes  to the approved  use of the
subject  property.  Furthermore,  CEQA  does not apply  to projects  which  a public  agency  rejects  or
disapproves  pursuant  to Section  15270(a).

shipment  to a final  off-site  destination.

governinental  agencies).  Furthermore,  based  on staff's  research  and information  provided  by

processing/recycling  activities  is not  a legal,  nonconforming  use -  and,  as such,  must  be

SGMC  Prohibits  that Use at 8530 Alameda  Street:  The subject  property  is zoned  Industrial  Flex

  ASSERTION:  The  Director's  Determination  is unsupported  by the South  Gate  Municipal

  The  appellant  first  argues  that  the  Director  failed  to make  a determination  that  the  legal,

  distinguish  between  primary  and ancillary  legal,  non-confornning  uses.  Rather,  the Director
  accepted  the appellants  assertion  that the storage  of truck  trailers  at the site was an "integral  part
  of metal  processing  operations,"  however,  the Director  did determine  that the truck  trailer  storage
  was only  done  as part  of the recycling/metal  processing  activities  while  those  activities  were
  occurring.  The Director  correctly  determined  that the current  use of the site for truck trailer  storage

  The City's  requirement  that the legal,  nonconforming  use be terminated  for 2 continuous  years

  storage  that is currently  occurring  has never been lawfully  approved  by the City.  This hearing  is
  not the venue to challenge  the City's  prior  Zoning  Code amendments  related  to permitted  uses.

  ASSERTION:  The  City  has Not  Considered  the  Environmental  Consequences  Resulting
  from  the  Termination  of  the  Existing  Land  Use  in  Favor  of  alternative  Land  Uses
  Inconsistent  with  the Requirements  of CEQA.
  The appellant  incorrectly  asserts that the City's  termination  of the legal, nonconforming  use of the
  subject  property  is tantamount  to changing  a land  use designation  - and would  require  review
  pursuant  to  the  California  Environmental  Quality  Act  ("CEQA").  However,  the  Director
  determined  that the actual use of the site for recycling/metal  processing  ceased in or about March
  2020  -  and  the  Director's  Determination  merely  is  a  confirmation  of  the
  abandonment/discontinuance  of the use of the site for recycling/metal  processing  by the owner.

  determined  and occur  at the time a conforming  use is proposed  by the appellant  or other interested

  CONCLUSION
  Staff  recommends  the Planning  Commission  uphold  the Director's  Determination  that the legal,

  its legal,  nonconforming  status, and all subsequent  uses of the property  shall  conform
  to current  provisions  of the South  Gate Zoning  Code.

  9.  The Director  sufficiently  considered  the factors  set forth in SGMC  11.55.040(D)  in the
  determination  that the recycling/metal  processing  use at the Subject  Property  had been

  Re: 8530 Alameda Street – Appeal of Director’s Denial of TUP Extension

Dear Chairperson Delgado, and Honorable Members of the City Planning Commission,

  Our firm represents Alameda Engle Properties, LLC (“AEP”), the owners of real
property located at 8530 Alameda Street in City of South Gate (“City”), California (the
“Property”).

  AEP historically operated a recycling facility on the Property, including storage of
truck trailers, since the early 1970s. Fleet Yards, Inc. (“Fleet Yards”) is the current
tenant on the Property, and has been storing truck trailers on the Property since 2020.
The truck trailer storage use has been continuous on the Property during the AEP
operations and subsequent Fleet Yards operations. As a family-owned business and
longstanding member of the South Gate community, AEP is dedicated to working
alongside its neighbors, fellow stakeholders, and the City to amicably resolve the City’s
concerns regarding historic uses on the Property.

  We are writing to clarify the scope and nature of the operations on the Property
and respectfully request that:

  a. The City acknowledge the existing legal nonconforming use; and
  b. The City allow Fleet Yards to continue its truck trailer storage operations
  pursuant to that use; or
  c. In the alternative, that the City honor its previous commitments regarding
  the TUP extensions in light of City staff’s error in requiring the TUP.

   1. Background

  At the recommendation of Joe Perez, the Director of Community Development at
the time, on July 16, 2020, Fleet Yards obtained a Temporary Use Permit (“TUP”) for
truck trailer use on the Property, subject to six conditions. The City made several
commitments to AEP and to Fleet Yards during the discussions leading to the TUP,
including that the TUP would be extended annually and that the City would consider
additional extensions in the future. The purpose of the TUP was to allow the City to
explore its priorities for development of education facilities at or around the Property.
We understand that many of these projects have been substantially delayed because of
setbacks caused by the COVID-19 Pandemic, changing real estate market conditions,
declining attendance for in-person academic programs, and environmental conditions in
the Property vicinity. On December 20, 2022, the current Community Development
Director informed Fleet Yards that the City would no longer consider the TUP extension
because of the City’s misapplication of the South Gate Municipal Code (“SGMC”) and
because the conditions of approval have been violated. On January 26, 2023, AEP
informed the City that they would be appealing the determination.1

  2. Truck Trailer Storage is a Legal & Nonconforming Use at the Property

  a. The City has Authority to Remedy the Previous Administration’s
  Errant Requirements for a TUP.

  The SGMC states that “nonconforming industrial uses may continue in use in any
zone where they were legally established.” SGMC § 11.55.030.E. AEP, and later, Fleet
Yards have been operating a recycling facility, including truck trailer storage at the
Property since the early 1970s. Fleet Yards obtained a TUP only at the City’s direction
and recommendations as a demonstration of their good faith efforts to comply with City
policies and procedures. The original TUP and TUP extensions were not necessary
because the truck trailer storage is an ongoing legal nonconforming use with over 50
years of history between the two operators on the Property. Fleet Yards agreed to the
TUP only to demonstrate its willingness to work with the City regarding a shared vision
for additional education facilities in South Gate. We understand that the zoning on the
Property was only recently changed to “Industrial Flex.”

  We also understand that the City’s did not issue certificates of occupancy
regularly during the early 1970s when the operations started at the Property. However,
we have attached the following documents that establish consistent storage of tractor
trailers long before the zone change on the Property:

  •  A July 1, 2019, Business License to Jack Engle authorizing “outside
  storage” at 8530 Alameda Street since April 18, 1977;2

  b. The Legal Nonconforming Use has Not Been Abandoned or
  Discontinued, and the Right to Continue is Protected and
  Preserved Pursuant to the South Gate Municipal Code.

  The SGMC states that a legal nonconforming industrial use is preserved so long
as it is not abandoned or discontinued for two consecutive calendar years. SGMC §
11.55.040.B. In determining whether a legal nonconforming use has been abandoned,
the Director is to evaluate (i) the apparent intent of the owner to discontinue, (ii) whether
furnishings equipment, or personal property have been removed, (iii) whether the use
has been discontinued for a period of two years, (iv) whether there is an active business
license and State Board of Equalization permit, and (v) whether there are active utilities
accounts, including electricity, gas, water, and waste collection. SGMC §
11.55.040.D.1-2.

  The SGMC specifically preserves legal nonconforming uses during transfers of
ownership or tenancy. SGMC § 11.55.040.E. Although there are limitations on
expansion, the nonconforming use provisions of the SGMC protect all established legal
nonconforming uses under the code, regardless of the scope of the use.6 There is no
language in the SGMC indicating that a portion of a legal nonconforming use is
abandoned due to the scope of the use at the time it is established.7 The South Gate
General Plan’s Community Design Element (“General Plan”) specifically anticipates
legal nonconforming uses in the South Gate College District given the existing
surrounding industrial uses. The General Plan also specifically requires that
“[i]ndustrial and manufacturing uses should remain in the area” until such time that the
college district expands. 8 (emphasis added).

  Here, between the two operations on the Property, truck trailer storage has been
a continuous use at the Property since 1973 -- notwithstanding hardships caused by the

  3. Terminating the Legal Nonconforming Use Violates the Doctrine of
  Equitable Estoppel

  The Doctrine of Equitable Estoppel was designed to promote fair and equitable
business transactions. The doctrine is based on the principle that a party who has
made a promise should be held accountable for it where reliance on the agreement was
reasonable, and enforcement of the agreement is necessary to avoid injustice.
Drennan v. Star Paving Co. (1958) 51 Cal.2d 409, 412-413; Garcia v. World Sav. &
Loan Assn. (2010) 183 Cal.App.4th 1031,1037. Here, Fleet Yards only agreed to the
TUP as a demonstration of good faith and willingness to work with the City regarding its
vision for the community. Based on communications from City staff on July 8, 2020, in
addition to the plain language of the TUP, the City was to consider additional extensions
of the TUP in addition to the initial five-year term. In addition, both AEP and Fleet Yards
agreed to the TUP as a measure of good faith and willingness to work with the City. It is
inequitable for the City to renege on this agreement. AEP forwent multiple lucrative
opportunities to sell the Property in reliance on the City’s communications and the
reasonable expectation that the City’s permits, licenses, and representations are
consistent notwithstanding changes in staff, changes in departmental priorities, and
unilateral changes to the zoning code. If the City does not honor its prior commitments,
both AEP and Fleet Yards will suffer substantial financial harm. In addition, this
inconsistency in City policies discourages investment in our community and is a
substantial deviation from the City’s treatment of similarly situated legacy businesses.

  4. Conclusion

  For the reasons stated above, the equitable path forward is to acknowledge truck
trailer storage on the Property as a preserved, legal nonconforming use in light of the
substantial evidence supporting this finding, and the requirements of the General Plan.
In the alternative, we respectfully request that the City reverse the Director’s denial of
the TUP extension. We understand that the City’s position is that the TUP was issued in
error. However, where, as here, immediately terminating the TUP causes substantial
harm to the community, and there is substantial evidence supporting that the use is
legal and nonconforming, we urge you to use this opportunity to make it right. As a
further demonstration of good faith and willingness to work together, we respectfully
request the City share any documentation indicating that the truck trailer storage is not
authorized pursuant to the legacy operations on the Property, and procedures for
obtaining a business permit zoning clearance where, as here, the use is legal
nonconforming.

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION
In accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the Director’s
determination qualifies for a categorical exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15321, (Class
21) “Enforcement Actions by Regulatory Agencies,” in that the City is enforcing the South Gate
Municipal Code.

The Planning Commission’s determination on the termination of the legal, non-conforming use of
the subject property is not subject to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review
because it is not an “approval” as defined in California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Section
15352, but rather a determination of whether a use must terminate at a site, and therefore does not
commit the City to any definite course of action regarding new uses or changes to the approved
use of the subject property. Furthermore, CEQA does not apply to projects which a public agency
rejects or disapproves pursuant to Section 15270(a).

BACKGROUND
This is an appeal by the applicant, Somos Law Group (“Somos”), on behalf of the property owner,
Alameda Engle Properties, LLC (“AEP” represented by Jason Engle), for a 6.78-acre property
located at 8530 Alameda Street. Somos is appealing the Director of Community Development’s
decision that the legal, nonconforming use for metal processing and/or recycling activities at the
subject property has been abandoned and can no longer be conducted, and the use of the site for
truck trailer storage as a principal use unrelated to metal processing/recycling activities is not a
legal, nonconforming use and must be immediately terminated. Somos is also requesting to change
the zoning of the subject property from IF (Industrial Flex) to M3 (Heavy Manufacturing) and
remove the subject property from the South Gate College District as shown in the Community
Design Element of the General Plan.

It should be noted that AEP also owns the abutting 2.9-acre site to the north at 8440 S. Alameda
Street, which is located outside of the City and in the County of Los Angeles. Access to both
properties is via a driveway from Alameda Street to the property at 8440 S. Alameda Street. This
property is also being used for truck trailer storage and according to County staff, a conditional
use permit (CUP) is currently being processed.

History of Zoning and Land Use of Subject Property
As early as 1961, the Subject Property was designated as being within a Heavy Manufacturing
(“M-3”) Zone.

 Based upon a review of public records and documents submitted by AEP, the Site was used by
Jack Engel & Company (hereinafter, “JECO”) and/or AEP for a metal processing/recycling facility
from as early as 1973 until approximately March 2020. During that time, the site was developed
with a single-story industrial structure used for the recycling operations conducted by JECO and/or
AEP.

The metal recycling operations conducted by JECO and/or AEP included, but was not limited to,
the delivery of scrap metal product to the Site inside of truck trailers – which would remain on site
for up to several months while the scrap metal was sorted and processed on-site, and prepared for
shipment to a final off-site destination.

In 1988, the City amended its Zoning Code, in part, to require a Conditional Use Permit for
recycling facilities. Thereafter, on or about April 28, 2015, the City Council adopted Ordinance
2323, which further amended the Zoning Code and changed the zoning classification of the Subject
Property to Industrial Flex (“IF”) Zone.

Pursuant to the Section 11.21.030 and Table 11.21-3 of the amended Zoning Code, recycling
facilities require a Conditional Use Permit – however, the recycling operations at the Subject
Property were deemed to be a legal, nonconforming land use that was allowed to continue in
accordance with SGMC Chapter 11.55 (“Nonconforming Uses and Buildings”).

According to public records and information submitted by AEP and/or its representatives, all metal
recycling operations ceased in or around March 2020 and are no longer being conducted at the
Site.

AEP has confirmed that around March 2020, Fleet Yards, Inc. commenced utilizing the Site solely
for the storage of truck trailers and/or containers as a principal use. Moreover, the structure that
was previously utilized to conduct the metal recycling at the Site was demolished.

In July 2020, the City approved Fleet Yards, Inc.’s application for a Temporary Use Permit and
issued TUP2020-01, authorizing the use of the Subject Property for “truck trailer storage for a one-
year period of time with possible extensions up to a maximum period of five years from the date
of approval”. TUP2020-01 expired on July 16, 2021, without a timely request for renewal from
Fleet Yards, Inc.

In December 2022, the Director advised Fleet Yards, Inc. that several conditions of approval of
the TUP had not been adhered to, and, moreover, that the TUP was ineligible for renewal as SGMC
§11.51.070(B)(4) sets the maximum duration of Temporary Use Permits to no more than three
days in a row or ten working days in any calendar year.

On May 2, 2023, the Planning Commission upheld the Director’s Determination to deny an
extension of the TUP (as set forth in Resolution 2023-05).

Notwithstanding the issuance and subsequent ineligibility for renewal of the TUP, the appellant
contended that the truck trailer storage activities are a legal, non-conforming use. As the appellant
bears the burden of proving the legal, nonconforming status of the truck trailer storage, Staff

ANALYSIS:

Appeal of Director’s Determination
On January 21, 2025, the City sent a Director’s Determination and Noncompliance Notification
letter to the applicant indicating the legal, nonconforming use of the Subject Property for metal
processing and/or recycling activities – including the integral truck trailer storage component of
those activities – has been determined to be abandoned and can no longer be conducted at the Site
unless otherwise in conformity to all current laws and regulations of the City (and applicable
governmental agencies). Furthermore, based on staff’s research and information provided by
Somos, the use of the Site for truck trailer storage as a principal use unrelated to metal
processing/recycling activities is not a legal, nonconforming use – and, as such, must be
immediately terminated.

On February 6, 2025, the applicant filed an appeal requesting the Planning Commission
challenging the Director’s determination based on the following grounds:

1. The Director’s Determination is unsupported by the South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC)
  purportedly due to the Director’s differentiation between an ancillary and primary use, that the
  immediate termination of a legal, nonconforming use is inconsistent with the SGMC and
  General Plan, and the Determination violates procedural requirements;
2. Substantive and procedural due process concerns; and
3. Termination of a legal, nonconforming use is a de facto regulatory taking; and,
4. The City’s failure to comply with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), Public
  Resources Code Section 21000, et seq.

Truck Storage/Terminal Use: AEP and its tenant have been using the subject property to store
trucks, truck-trailers, and storage containers. Under the SGMC, this use is defined as “truck
storage/terminal” use which, pursuant to the SGMC Section 11.60.230 “T” definitions, “means
indoor or outdoor site for freight, truck terminals, truck storage yards, or similar commercial
facilities.”

SGMC Prohibits that Use at 8530 Alameda Street: The subject property is zoned Industrial Flex
(IF). Table 11.21-3, under SGMC Section 11.21.030 “Land use permissions tables,” lists allowed
land uses within the IF zone. Truck storage/terminal use is not listed on that Table as an allowed

  322
   use within the IF zone. SGMC Section 11.21.020 notes that “Any land use that is not specifically
  listed in the land use tables for the applicable zone shall not be allowed or permitted within the
  zone.” Therefore, the storage of trucks, truck-trailers and containers is a prohibited use in the IF
  zone.

  It is undisputed that the recycling/metal processing activities that occurred at the subject property
  were legal, nonconforming, and that truck trailer storage is not currently a permitted use at the
  subject property pursuant to the South Gate Municipal Code (inclusive of the Zoning Code). The
  issues of contention are (i) whether the legal, nonconforming recycling/metal processing activities
  at the subject property have been abandoned; and/or (ii) whether the appellant has submitted
  sufficient evidence to substantiate that the current use of the site for truck trailer storage unrelated
  to recycling/metal processing activities constitutes a legal, nonconforming use of the subject
  property.

  In response to the appellant’s arguments set forth in the Request for Appeal, Staff submits the
  following.

  ASSERTION: The Director’s Determination is unsupported by the South Gate Municipal
  Code.
  The appellant first argues that the Director failed to make a determination that the legal,
  nonconforming use is “wholly discontinued or abandoned for a continuous period of two calendar
  years” as required by SGMC 11.55.040(D). The Director, however, correctly determined that the
  legal, nonconforming recycling/metal processing use at the site was wholly discontinued and/or
  abandoned – as evidenced by the cessation of all activities associated with the recycling/metal
  processing activities in or around 2020, including the demolition of the structure that was
  previously utilized for such activities. Contrary to the appellant’s contention, the Director did not
  distinguish between primary and ancillary legal, non-conforming uses. Rather, the Director
  accepted the appellants assertion that the storage of truck trailers at the site was an “integral part
  of metal processing operations,” however, the Director did determine that the truck trailer storage
  was only done as part of the recycling/metal processing activities while those activities were
  occurring. The Director correctly determined that the current use of the site for truck trailer storage
  only is NOT a continuation of the use of the trucks for the recycling/metal processing activities,
  and, is, in fact, a wholly new use.

  The appellant also argues that the immediate termination of the truck trailer storage is inconsistent
  with the South Gate Municipal Code and the General Plan – which the appellant contends promotes
  a more gradual transition to a conforming use. However, the appellant fails to recognize that it
  was the appellant’s abandonment of the recycling/metal processing activities for more than 2 years
  that resulted in the termination of its legal, nonconforming rights – and not any action by the City.
  The City’s requirement that the legal, nonconforming use be terminated for 2 continuous years
  does, in fact, provide for a gradual transition – but the appellant failed to utilize those 2 years to
  make a transition to a conforming use. Instead, the appellant transitioned to using the subject
  property for the prohibited truck trailer storage use.

AS13772.0860893 4909-8288-0805v1
   The appellant further mistakenly argues that the Director failed to make findings required by
  Section 11.55.040(D) of the municipal code. Specifically, the appellant argues that the Director
  failed to consider and make a determination regarding (i) the property owner’s intent; (ii) the
  presence or absence of personal property associated with the legal, nonconforming use; (iii)
  presence or absence of furnishings, equipment, and other property associated with the use; and,
  (iv) continuity of utility service to the property.

  The appellant incorrectly interprets SGMC §11.55.040(D). Pursuant to SGMC §11.55.040(D)(1),
  in order to determine whether a property owner has abandoned/discontinued a legal,
  nonconforming use, the Director is required to determine the “apparent intent of the owner to
  discontinue use of the nonconforming structure is apparent, as determined by the director”
  (emphasis added). This particular requirement, however, is applicable to the intent to
  discontinue/abandon a nonconforming structure – and not the owner’s intent to discontinue a legal,
  nonconforming use. That being said, the Director determined that the structure previously existing
  at the site was voluntarily demolished in or around March 2020 – and that all other activities
  associated with the recycling/metal processing use also terminated around the same time. The
  Director also determined that all other equipment, furnishings, and the structure itself used for the
  recycling/metal processing activities have been absent from the site for more than two years.
  Moreover, no additional business licenses have been acquired for recycling/metal processing
  activities for at least 2 years. Any continued utility use at the site (including electricity, gas, water
  or waste collection) does not negate the Director’s determination that all use of the subject property
  for recycling/metal processing activities has been abandoned/discontinued for more than 2 years.

  ASSERTION: The City’s management of the legal nonconforming use gives rise to
  substantive and procedural due process concerns.
  The appellant contends that the manner in which the City has handled requests from appellant’s
  legal counsel has raised concerns regarding the appellant’s substantive and procedural due process.
  Appellant also apparently incorrectly argues that the Director suggested that the appellant was
  required to obtain a Conditional Use Permit in 1988 as a result of a change in the City’s Zoning
  Code. Lastly, appellant argues that Staff has been slow to acknowledge or process its request for
  a Zone Change and General Plan Amendment. It should be noted that Staff provided documents
  in its possession – however, was not required to provide copies of business licenses which were
  no longer in the possession of the City. [Business licenses are issued to business operators – and
  the appellant would have been in the best position to retain the prior business licenses.] Moreover,
  the Director did not assert that the appellant required a Conditional Use Permit, but rather that the
  change in the City’s Zoning Code requiring a Conditional Use Permit for the recycling/metal
  processing use of the site is what converted the legal status of recycling/metal processing use of
  the site to “legal, nonconforming”. Lastly, the processing of the Zone Change and General Plan
  Amendment is a separate matter before the Planning Commission, and arguments related to the
  processing of those requests are not related to the Director’s Determination regarding the
  termination of the legal, nonconforming status of the recycling/metal processing activities or the
  lack of such status for the truck trailer storage.

  ASSERTION: Termination of the legal nonconforming use is a de facto regulatory taking.
  The appellant contends that the changes to the City’s Zoning laws and General Plan amount to a
  regulatory taking because of the limited uses allowed at the subject property. However, the City
  provides for the continuation of nonconforming uses – and, as such, appellant would have been
  allowed to continue the recycling/metal processing use of the site had the appellant not abandoned
  the use or otherwise caused the termination of the use as set forth in SGMC Chapter 11.55. It is

   the appellant’s actions that have resulted in the termination of the ability to continue conducting
  recycling/metal processing activities – and it is the Director’s determination that the truck trailer
  storage that is currently occurring has never been lawfully approved by the City. This hearing is
  not the venue to challenge the City’s prior Zoning Code amendments related to permitted uses.

  ASSERTION: The City has Not Considered the Environmental Consequences Resulting
  from the Termination of the Existing Land Use in Favor of alternative Land Uses
  Inconsistent with the Requirements of CEQA.
  The appellant incorrectly asserts that the City’s termination of the legal, nonconforming use of the
  subject property is tantamount to changing a land use designation – and would require review
  pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”). However, the Director
  determined that the actual use of the site for recycling/metal processing ceased in or about March
  2020 – and the Director’s Determination merely is a confirmation of the
  abandonment/discontinuance of the use of the site for recycling/metal processing by the owner.
  Although the commencement of a new conforming use may require CEQA review, that would be
  determined and occur at the time a conforming use is proposed by the appellant or other interested
  party – however, Staff has determined that this appeal is exempt from CEQA review.

  Staff recommends that the Planning Commission uphold the Director’s determination based on the
  findings in the attached resolution.

  CONCLUSION
  Staff recommends the Planning Commission uphold the Director’s Determination that the legal,
  nonconforming use of the subject property for metal processing and/or recycling activities has
  been abandoned for more than two (2) continuous years, and can no longer be conducted at the
  site; and that the use of the site for truck trailer storage as a principal use unrelated to metal
  processing/recycling activities is not a legal, nonconforming use.

  3.  Terminatinq  the Leqal  Nonconforminq  Use Violates  the Doctrine  of
  Equitable  Estoppel

  The Doctrine of Equitable Estoppel was designed to promote fair and equitable
business transactions.  The doctrine is based on the principle that a party who has
made a promise should be held accountable  for it where reliance on the agreement  was
reasonable,  and enforcement  of the agreement  is necessary  to avoid injustice.
Drennan v Star Paving Co. (1958) 51 Cal.2d 409, 412-41 3; Garcia v World Sav &
Loan Assn. (2010) 183 Cal.App.4th  1031, 4 037. Here, Fleet Yards only agreed to the
TUP as a demonstration  of good faith and willingness  to work with the City regarding  its
vision for the community.  Based on communications  from City staff on July 8, 2020, in
addition to the plain language of the TUP, the City was to consider additional extensions
of the TUP in addition to the initial five-year term. In addition, both AEP and Fleet Yards
agreed to the TUP as a measure of good faith and willingness  to work with the City. It is
inequitable  for the City to renege on this agreement.  AEP forwent multiple lucrative
opportunities  to sell the Property in reliance on the City's communications  and the
reasonable  expectation  that the City's permits, licenses, and representations  are
consistent  notwithstanding  changes in staff, changes in departmental  priorities, and
unilateral changes to the zoning code. If the City does not honor its prior commitments,
both AEP and Fleet Yards will suffer substantial  financial harm. In addition, this
inconsistency  in City policies discourages  investment  in our community  and is a
substantial  deviation from the City's treatment  of similarly situated legacy businesses.

  4.  Conclusion

  For the reasons stated above, the equitable path forward is to acknowledge  truck
trailer storage on the Property as a preserved,  legal nonconforming  use in light of the
substantial  evidence supporting  this finding, and the requirements  of the General Plan.
In the alternative,  we respectfully  request that the City reverse the Director's denial of
the TUP extension.  We understand  that the City's position is that the TUP was issued in
error. However, where, as here, immediately  terminating  the TUP causes substantial
harm to the community,  and there is substantial  evidence supporting  that the use is
legal and nonconforming,  we urge you to use this opportunity  to make it right. As a
further demonstration  of good faith and willingness  to work together, we respectfully
request the City share any documentation  indicating that the truck trailer storage is not
authorized  pursuant to the legacy operations  on the Property, and procedures  for
obtaining a business permit zoning clearance where, as here, the use is legal
nonconforming.

 made a promise should be held accountable  for it where reliance on the agreement  was
 reasonable,  and enforcement  of the agreement  is necessary  to avoid injustice.

the City Attorney's  Office  at the May 2, Planning Commission  meeting  and reiterated  below, an appeal of this
matter to the City Council  is not available.

As the City has repeatedly  advised AEP and Fleet Yards, the TUP was initially  issued in error, because it
purported  to allow a "temporary"  use of the Premises for a period of at least one year and possibly as many as
five years, far in excess of the limited  duration  mandated  by the Zoning Code. Temporary  use permits,  as the
name implies, are intended  to allow only short-term  uses of land.  Specifically,  Section 11.51.070  of the  Zoning

Code states that the maximum  duration  of a temporary  use permit  shall not exceed three days in a row or ten
days in any calendar  year.  It is unfortunate  that the TUP was erroneously  issued in 2020 for a much longer one-
year period and erroneously  renewed  in 2021 for an additional  one-year  period.  But those earlier errors do not
entitle AEP to further  extensions  of the TUP for periods  far in excess of the maximum  durations  authorized  by
the Zoning Code. Simply put, there is no authority  in the Zoning Code for issuing or renewing  a temporary  use

permit for any period longer than three consecutive  days or ten days in any calendar year.

Furthermore,  the original  issuance of the TUP in violation  of the Zoning Code aiso meant that the City was not
required  to grant AEP a hearing on the matter  of renewing  the TUP. Again, as publicly stated by the City's legal
counsel at the Planning Commission  meeting,  the City granted  that hearing as a matter  of courtesy  - something
that was also explained  to AEP in the course of the May 2 meeting.  No hearing was required  because no
decision by the Planning Commission  could have resulted  in validation  and extension  of the TUP. Section
11.51.020  of the Zoning Code states that any permit  conflicting  with the provisions  of the Zoning Code "shall  be

On May 2, 2023, the South  Gate Planning  Commission  conducted  a public  hearing  on the request  by Alameda
Engle Properties,  LLC's ("AEP")  to extend,  for a period  of one year, the term  of Temporary  Use Permit  No. 2020-
01 (the "TUP").  Such an extension  would  have allowed  the continued  storage  of trucks  and truck-trailers  at 8530
Alameda  Street  (the "Premises")  by AEP"s tenant,  Fleet Yards, Inc. ("Fleet  Yards").  At the conclusion  of that
hearing,  the Planning  Commission  upheld  the City's earlier  decision  to deny the extension  and not renew  the
TUP. AEP has now asked to appeal that decision  to the South Gate City Council.  For the reasons  explained  by
the City Attorney's  Office  at the May 2, Planning  Commission  meeting  and reiterated  below,  an appeal  of this
matter  to the City Council  is not available.

As the City has repeatedly  advised  AEP and Fleet Yards, the TUP was initially  issued in error,  because  it
purported  to allow  a "temporary"  use of the Premises  for a period  of at least one year and possibly  as many as
five years, far in excess of the limited  duration  mandated  by the Zoning  Code.  Temporary  use permits,  as the
name implies,  are intended  to allow only short-term  uses of land.  Specifically,  Section 11.51.070  of the Zoning
Code states that the maximum  duration  of a temporary  use permit  shall not exceed  three  days in a row or ten
days in any calendar  year.  It is unfortunate  that the TUP was erroneously  issued in 2020 for a much  longer  one-
year period  and erroneously  renewed  in 2021 for an additional  one-year  period.  But those  earlier  errors  do not
entitle  AEP to further  extensions  of the TUP for periods  far in excess of the maximum  durations  authorized  by
the Zoning Code.  Simply  put, there  is no authority  in the Zoning  Code for issuing or renewing  a temporary  use
permit  for any period  longer  than three  consecutive  days or ten days in any calendar  year.

Furthermore,  the original  issuance  of the TUP in violation  of the Zoning  Code also meant  that the City was not
required  to grant AEP a hearing  on the matter  of renewing  the TUP. Again,  as publicly  stated  by the City's legal
counsel  at the Planning  Commission  meeting,  the City granted  that  hearing  as a matter  of courtesy  - something
that was also explained  to AEP in the course  of the May 2 meeting.  No hearing  was required  because  no
decision  by the Planning  Commission  could have resulted  in validation  and extension  of the TUP. Section
11.51.020  of the Zoning  Code states that  any permit  conflicting  with  the provisions  of the Zoning  Code "shall  be
null and void."  Both the TUP and the requested  one-year  extension  conflict  with the provisions  of the Zoning

SUBJECT: APPEAL OF THE DIRECTOR OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT'S DECISION TO
DENY AN EXTENSION OF TEMPORARY USE PERMIT NO. 2020-01 FOR TRUCK TRAILER
STORAGE AT 8530 ALAMEDA STREET.

PURPOSE: Public hearing to consider an appeal of the Director of Community Development's decision to deny
an extension of Temporary Use Pe1mit (TUP) No. 2020-01 for truck-trailer storage at 8530 Alameda Street, South
Gate.

RECOMMENDED ACTION:
1. CONDUCT a public heating pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code Table 11.51-1 and Section 11.50.040.B;
2. ACCEPT the dete1mination that this matter is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act;
3. ADOPT the findings as outlined in Resolution No. 2023-02 (Attachment A); and
4. UPHOLD the decision of the Director of Community Development denying an extension of TUP No. 2020-
  01 by adopting Resolution No. 2023-05.

PUBLIC NOTIFICATION: Advertising and notification of the public heating for this item was conducted in
compliance with Sections 11.50.020 and 11.50.030 of the South Gate Municipal Code ("SGMC"). Notices of the
hearing were posted and published in the "South Gate Press" on February 9, April 6 and April 20, 2023.

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION: The California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA"), codified at
California Public Resources Code§§ 21000 et seq., requires the City to consider the potential environmental
impacts of any project which the City is asked to approve. State regulations known as the "CEQA Guidelines",
codified at Division 6 of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations, provide a number of "categorical
exemptions" for activities which are not deemed to be projects under CEQA or which are otherwise not subject
to CEQA. In the present case, the matter before the City Council is exempt from CEQA pursuant to a Class l
exemption set forth in Section 15301 of the CEQA Guidelines. Class 1 exemptions apply to the operation, repair,
maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities,
mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of existing or fo1mer use.
Here, the Planning Commission is being asked to approve or deny a license to continue the existing or former use
of the licensed facility and is therefore a matter covered by the Class l exception.

BACKGROUND: This is an appeal by Jason Engle on behalf of Alameda Engle Properties, LLC, the owner of
property located at 8530 Alameda Street. Mr. Engle is appealing the Director of Community Development's
decision to deny an extension or renewal of Temporary Use Permit 2020-01. The history of that Temporary Use
Permit is as follows:

The City's Business License Department shows business license records (Attachment B) for "Jack Engle Co,"
which statted business on Ap1il 18, 1977, and closed business on March 27, 2020, at 8530 Alameda Street. This
business type was listed as a "Manufacturing - Metal" business with "outside storage only." The appellant and
its predecessor had previously been utilizing the property to operate a metal recycling facility, in addition to the
ancillary storage of truck containers and truck trailers.

Upon closing that business, the appellant continued to utilize the site by leasing the prope1ty to tenants for the 417
 outside  storage  of truck  trailers  and tiuck  containers.  In order to do so, the applicant  applied  for, and received,
Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01.  That permit  "permitted  the use of truck trailer  storage  for a one year period  with
possible  one year extensions  up to a maximum  period  of five years from  the date of approval,  at 8530 Alameda
Street,"  with  six conditions  of approval.  A July  16, 2020  letter  from  the City's  former  Director  of Community
Development,  setting  forth  those conditions  of approval  for that pertnit,  is attached  hereto  as Attachment  C. As
of the appeal date, the appellant  has failed  to comply  with  the required  conditions  of approval  and has also been
operating  without  a city business  license.

The  appellant  applied  for  a "renewal"  of Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01  on July  11, 2022.  For the reasons
explained  below,  the City's  current  Director  of Community  Development  declined  to renew  the permit.  This
appeal  followed.  The City  Manager's  January  12, 2023  letter  to the appellant,  and the appellant's  January  26,
2023 letter in response,  both pertain  to that appeal  and are attached  here to as Attachment  D and Attachment  E.

ANALYSIS:  The renewal  application  was denied  because under  the SGMC:  (1) the use which  is the subject  of
the  Temporary  Use  Permit  is prohibited  at 8530  Alameda;  and (2) Temporary  Use Permits  can only  allow
otherwise  unauthorized  uses to be conducted  for a few days, not for multi-year  periods.

Past/Proposed  Use of Property  is as a "Truck  Storage/Terminal":  Applicant  and its tenant  have been using  the
subject  property  to store trucks,  truck-trailers,  and storage  containers.  Under  the SGMC,  this use is defined  as
"truck  storage/terminal"  use which,  pursuant  to the SGMC  Section  11.60.230  "T"  definitions,  "means  indoor  or
outdoor  site for freight,  truck  terminals,  truck  storage  yards,  or similar  commercial  facilities."

SGMC  Prohibits  that Use at 8530 Alameda  Street:  The subject  property  is zoned  Industrial  Flex  (IF).  Table
11.21-3,  under  SGMC  Section  11.21.030  "Land  use pernnissions  tables",  lists  allowed  land uses within  the IF
zone. Truck  storage/teiminal  use is not listed  on that Table  as an allowed  use within  the IF zone.  SGMC  Section
11.21.020  notes that "Any  land use that is not specifically  listed in the land use tables for the applicable  zone shall
not be allowed  or permitted  within  the zone."  Therefore,  the storage  of trucks,  truck-trailers  and containers  is a
prohibited  use in the IF zone.

Temporary  Use Pertnits  Cannot  Authorize  Prohibited  Uses for Extended  Durations.  Pursuant  to SGMC  Section
11.51.070  "Temporary  Use Permit,"  temporary  use permits  are processed  administratively  to "allow  for short-
term  activities  that warrant  individual  consideration  and are acceptable  because  of their  temporary,  short-tertn
nature."  SGMC  Section  11.51.070  (A) "Temporary  Uses,"  also notes  that the "provisions  of this section  shall
regulate  all special  events  and temporary  land  uses as permitted  by Table  11.21-3,  11.21-4,  or 11.21-5,  as
applicable  to the zone, or as determined  by the director."  SGMC  Section  11.51.010  (B) lists "Mandatory  Approval
Conditions"  for temporary  use permits,  wherein  there are "limits  on the maximum  duration  will  be specified  in
the permit,  and shall not exceed three days in a row,  or ten working  days in any calendar  year."

Original  Issuance  of the TUP was Done in Error,  and Renewal  of the TUP is not authorized  by the SGMC.  Based
on the aforementioned  reasoning,  the City's  current  Director  of Community  Development  determined  that the
City  would  not grant  an extension  of TUP 2020-01.  That Temporary  Use Permit  should  never have been issued
in the first place,  since it purported  to authorize  the subject  use for one or more years,  far longer  than the three-
consecutive-day  and ten-nonconsecutive-day  maximum  periods  authorized  by the SGMC.  The Director  and the
City  Manager  each communicated  that decision  to the appellant.  Appellant  has appealed  that decision,  which
appeal is the subject  of the above-referenced  hearing.

  418
 CONCLUSION: Staff believes the Director's decision to deny the applicant's request to extend Temporary Use
Permit 2020-01 is mandated by the SGMC. Staff recommends that the Planoing Commission uphold the
Director's decision and deny the appellant's request.

  I.  AEP’s operations are legal and have remained constant since 1973

  The SELA Letter suggests that the Site Operations have operated illegally for

specifically allowed to continue by the South Gate Municipal Code (“SGMC”). 1

  Legal nonconforming uses are not illegal; they are land uses or structures that
were lawful when they were established but no longer comply with the current zoning
regulations. Since 1973, Site Operations at the Property have been operating lawfully
and with City oversight. The City has issued multiple business licenses specially
authorizing outdoor storage – an authorized use on the Property.

error. Given the uses of the Property never changed and the legal nonconforming use
was maintained, no TUP should have been required in the first place. 2 Since the City’s
acknowledgement that the 2020 TUP was in error, AEP and its tenant (Fleet Yards)

City.

is used in lead alloys (e.g., for car batteries), wood preservatives (e.g., railroad ties),
and applications in the metallurgical, glass-making, and semiconductor industries. The
SELA Letter references a federal Environmental Protection Agency (“EPA”) study that
purportedly found that 83 homes adjacent to the Property exceeded California’s
standards for acceptable levels of arsenic. 3 From this, the SELA Letter makes the
unfounded suggestion that the AEP Operations or Property are responsible for this
arsenic. This is wholly unsubstantiated.

manufacturer. 4 In light of these facts, the SELA Letter’s suggestion that AEP, the Site
Operations, or the Property are responsible for any locally elevated arsenic levels is
unsubstantiated and inaccurate.

  III.  Continuing the Property’s legal nonconforming use is in the interests of
  the City, its citizens, and AEP

  We appreciate SELA’s acknowledgement that the City’s ongoing consideration of
the industrial policies and zoning requires time to carefully study and consider the
impacts of same. Despite its right to continue the legal nonconforming use, AEP is
actively trying to transition the Property to a use compatible with the Industrial Flex (“IF”)
zoning now in place. Permissible uses in the IF zone include civic/institutional facilities,
open space, office/research and development and light industrial uses.

  Given the industrial nature of the surrounding properties however, both in the City
as well as the County of Los Angeles, this transition is anticipated to require time and
resources. AEP’s support for this transition is funded by rental income received from
the Property’s current tenant, Fleet Yards. In order to minimize disruptions to the
redevelopment process and preserve AEP’s support for this transition, the current
legally nonconforming use of the Property must continue until such time as a proposal
for development of the Property consistent with the IF zone is received, or by 2035,
consistent with the requirements of the current General Plan.

  Prematurely terminating the currently legal use would not expedite the
redevelopment process, invites legal challenges, and would likely cause unnecessary
delays. Such delay benefits no one: not SELA; not the City; and certainly not he
citizens and business leaders of the South Gate community.

developmental problems in children. Without proper cleanup, these toxins

 Dear Honorable Planning Commission,  City Clerk, Mayor Davila, City Council, and City
Manager,

I am writing to express my strong support for upholding South Gate's municipal code in the case
of 8530 Alameda  Street and to urge the City Council to deny the appeal Tiled by the property
owner. From what I have gathered through the agenda and available information,  it is clear that
this is not a case of unfair treatment, but rather the City rightfully enforcing its zoning
regulations,  as it would for any other business or property owner.

The Facts: How We Got Here

For decades, 8530 Alameda Street was home to a metal processing and recycling facility. Even
affer zoning changes in 2015, the City allowed the business to continue under legal
nonconforming status, showing its willingness  to work with long-standing  businesses  and
provide flexibility for property owners.

However, that nonconforming  status required renewal, and in 2020, the property owner failed to
submit that renewal. As a result, the legal protection for that prior use expired, and the site
became subject to the current Industrial Flex (IF) zoning, which does not allow truck trailer
storage.

Despite this, the site has continued to be used For truck trailer storage, an operation that was
never separately recognized as a legal nonconforming use. The City is now requiring
compliance  with existing zoning, which is a necessary  and standard enforcement  action.

South Gate's Approach  Has Been Fair and Consistent

The City of South Gate has a proven history or working with its business community,  and this
case is no exception. The fact that the previous nonconforming use was allowed to continue for
nearly five years after the zoning change shows that the City was not looking to push
businesses  out but instead offered reasonable  opportunities  to transition.

However, zoning laws exist for a reason, and South Gate is simply applying the same standards
it would to any other business. The property owner had multiple opportunities  to maintain their
legal status but Failed to foilow the required renewal process. This is not an issue of the City
being unreasonable-this  is a case of a business  not following the necessary  steps to remain in
compliance.

  538
  Addressing  Arguments  Against the City's Decision

 Some may argue that truck storage was always part of the metal processing operation and
 therefore should still quali$ under the original nonconTorming status. However, the key issue is
 that nonconforming use protections do not extend indefinitely without proper renewal.

  The original nonconforming  status applied specifically  to metal processing, not to
 truck storage as a separate business.

  Once metal processing ceased and the structure was demolished, the truck
storage became an independent  operation-not a continuation of the original use.

  Under South Gate's current zoning regulations,  truck trailer storage is not a
permitted  use in the IF zone.

The  City is not changing the rules or targeting this specffic business. If noncompliant operations
were  allowed to continue indefinitely without proper renewal, it would undermine the entire
purpose  of zoning laws.

Addressing  Misinformation

I have also seen claims that the City is acting unfairly or even engaging in selective
enforcement.  However, from what I have read, South Gate has acted responsibly and
transparently in enforcing its municipal code,

This situation is not about the City suddenly changing its stance-it  is about a property owner
who failed to take the necessary steps to maintain their legal standing. It is misleading and
unfair to suggest that the City is at fault when all it is doing is enforcing the rules that apply to
everyone.

Why Denying the Appeal Is the Right Decision

South Gate's zoning regulations exist to ensure Fairness, order, and responsible land use. If the
City allows this appeal to succeed, it will set a dangerous precedent that nonconforming uses
can continue indefinitely, even when renewal requirements  are ignored. That would not be fair to
other businesses  and property owners who Follow the rules.

I urge the City Council to:

  539
 - Uphold the City's decision and deny the appeal to protect the integrity  of South  Gate's
municipal  code.

  Ensure that land use regulations are applied fairly and consistently to all businesses.

- Stand by the City's long-term planning and zoning vision rather than  allowing  businesses  to
bypass  regulations  through  legal  loopholes.

South Gate has done its part to support local businesses while also maintaining the integrity  of
its zoning regulations. Now, it is time to uphold those regulations and deny this appeal.

Thank you for your time and for your commitment to enforcing South Gate's municipal  code
fairly  and consistently.

Respectfully,

Nathan  Cueto

The applicant  is requesting  to change  the zoning  of the property  at 8530 Alameda  Street from  IF

future  growth  of the East Los Angeles  Community  College  ("ELACC")  within  the South  Gate
College  District  as described  in the Community  Design  Element  of the City's  General  Plan. The

  Dear HonorablePlanningCommission,City Clerk, Mayor Davila,City Council, and City
 Manager,

I am writing to express my strongsupportfor upholdingSouth Gate's municipal code in the case
of 8530 Alameda Street andto urge the City Councilto deny the appeal filed by the property
owner. From what I have gatheredthroughthe agenda and availableInformation,it is clear that
this is not a case of unfairtreatment,but rather the City rightfully enforcing its zoning
regulations,as it would for any other business or property owner.

The Facts: How We Got Here

For decades, 8530 AlamedaStreetwas home to a metal processingand recyclingfacility. Even
after zoning changes in 2015,the City allowed the business to continueunder legal
nonconformingstatus, showingits willingnessto work with long-standingbusinesses and
provide flexibility for property owners.

However,that nonconformingstatus required renewal, and in 2020, the propertyowner failed to
submit that renewal. As a result,the legal protectionfor that prior use expired, and the site
became subject to the currentJndustrialFlex (IF) zoning, which does not allow truck trailer
storage.

Despite this, the site has continuedto be used for truck trailer storage, an operationthat was
never separatelyrecognizedas a legal nonconforminguse. The City is now requiring
compliancewith existing zoning,which is a necessary and standardenforcementaction.

South Gate's Approach Has Been Fair and Consistent

The City of South Gate has a proven history of working with its business community,and this
case is no exception.The fact that the previous nonconforminguse was allowed to continue for
nearly five years after the zoning change shows that the City was not looking to push
businessesout but insteadoffered reasonable opportunities to transition.

However,zoning laws exist for a reason, and South Gate is simply app)ying the same standards
it wou)dto any other business.The property owner had multipleopportunitiesto maintain their
legal status but failed to followthe required renewal process. This is not an issue of the City
being unreasonabte-this is a case of a business not following the necessary steps to remain in
compliance.

  571
 Addressing  Arguments  Against the City's Decision

Some may argue that truck storage was always part of the metal processing operation and
therefore should still qualify under the original nonconforming status. However, the key issue is
 that nonconforming  use protections do not extend indefinitely  without proper renewal.

  -  The origina( nonconforming  status applied specifically  to metal processing,  not to
truck storage as a separate business.

  Once metal processing ceased and the structure was demolished, the truck
storage became an independent  operation-not a continuation of the original use.

  -  Under South Gate's current zoning regulations,  truck trailer storage is not a
permitted  use in the IF zone.

The City is not changing the ru(es or targeting this specific business. If noncompliant operations
were allowed to continue indefinitely without proper renewal, it would undermine the entire
purpose of zoning [aws.

Addressing  Misinformation

 l have also seen claims that the City is acting unfairly or even engaging in selective
enforcement.  However, from what I have read, South Gate has acted responsibly and
transparently in enforcing its municipal code.

This situation is not about the City suddenly  changing its stance-it  is about a property owner
who failed to take the necessary steps to maintain their legal standing. It is misleading and
unfair to suggest that the City is at fault when all it is doing is enforcing the rules that apply to
everyone.

Why Denying the Appeal Is the Right Decision

South Gate's zoning regulations  exist to ensure fairness,  order, and responsible  land use. If the
City allows this appeal to succeed, it will set a dangerous
  precedent that nonconforming uses
can continue indefinitely, even when renewal requirements are ignored. That would not be fair to
other businesses and property owners who follow the rules.

I urge the City Council to:

  572
 - Uphold the City's decision and deny the appeal to protect the integrity of South Gate's
municipal code.

- Ensure that land use regulations are applied fairly and consistently to all businesses.

- Stand by the City's long-term planning and zoning vision rather than allowing businesses to
bypass regulations through legal loopholes.

SouthGatehas doneits partto supportlocal businesses while also maintaining the integrity of
its zoning regulations. Now, it is time to uphold those regulations and deny this appeal,

Thank you for your time and for your commitment to enforcing South Gate's municipal  code
fairly and consistenUy.

Respectfully,

Nathan  Cueto

  PURPOSE:  To adopt  Resolutions  to preliminarily  approve  the Engineer's  Report,  to declare
  the City  of South  Gate's  ("City")  intention  to levy  and collect  assessments,  and to set a public
  hearing.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
